hook: Astronomers found 27 new worlds beyond Neptune, changing our understanding of the solar system.

sections.voiceover: Astronomers found 27 new worlds beyond Neptune, changing our understanding of the solar system.
sections.visual_cue: A map of the solar system with 27 new trans-Neptunian objects highlighted.
sections.sfx_cue: Sound of telescope zooming in on distant stars.

sections.voiceover: The smallest of these objects is only 3 miles wide.
sections.visual_cue: A timeline showing the discovery process, with the Hubble and James Webb telescopes highlighted.
sections.sfx_cue: Sound of telescopes turning and focusing.

sections.voiceover: These discoveries are changing our understanding of early solar system formation, but they also highlight the vastness of our solar system.
sections.visual_cue: A comparison chart showing the size of the smallest trans-Neptunian object against the size of a city block.
sections.sfx_cue: Sound of a question mark being raised.

sections.voiceover: These 27 new trans-Neptunian objects, the smallest of which is only 3 miles wide, were published in The Astronomical Journal on September 8, 2026.
sections.visual_cue: A diagram showing the orbit of one of the new trans-Neptunian objects.
sections.sfx_cue: Sound of a planet zooming in on screen.

sections.voiceover: These discoveries could help us find clues about how other planets form.
sections.visual_cue: A map of the solar system with a question mark over the 27 new trans-Neptunian objects.
sections.sfx_cue: Sound of a question mark being raised.
